# S02 — Core: registry and CLI adapters

The Go module, the project registry, and the slicer and adj adapters that
every later screen and the engine read through. No UI and no third-party
dependency (`plan.s02-cut`).

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:** any UI, any third-party module, git calls, and the daemon.

## Why

Every screen and the engine read slicer and adj only through their CLIs
(`boundaries.md`, TRACKING_RULE), and ork's own state starts with the
registry (`state.files`, `state.format`). Building this first, behind one
interface, lets S03 move it behind the daemon socket unchanged
(`dash.pre-daemon`).

## Files

- `go.mod`: module `github.com/squalor-xyz/ork`, `go 1.27.2`, matching
  adjudicate. No `require` lines.
- `internal/registry/`: load, validate, save and seed `projects.json`.
- `internal/clirun/`: run one CLI call with arguments, a deadline, and the
  captured stdout, stderr and exit code.
- `internal/slicercli/`: typed calls over the slicer CLI.
- `internal/adjcli/`: typed calls over the adj CLI.
- `internal/source/`: the `Source` interface the TUI and later the daemon
  use, and its direct implementation over the adapters.
- `testdata/cli/slicer/`, `testdata/cli/adj/`: recorded real output, with
  `testdata/cli/VERSIONS` naming the slicer and adj versions recorded.
- Every `.go` file starts with `// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later`.

## Failing tests

Write these first and watch them fail:
- registry: a round trip keeps every field in the docs/state.md example.
- registry: a file with an unknown `version` is refused with an error
  naming the version.
- registry: a save writes a temp file in the same directory and renames
  it; a failed write leaves the old file intact and no temp file behind.
- registry: when the file is missing, seeding writes only the decided
  projects (slicer, adjudicate, DataBall, agents) whose directories exist
  under the seed root, sets `adj` from whether `.adjudicate.json` exists
  there, and reports what it wrote (`registry.seed`).
- clirun: a call past its deadline returns a timeout error, and the child
  process group is killed.
- clirun: a non-zero exit keeps stdout and stderr verbatim; a slicer
  `{"error":{"code","message","command"}}` object on stdout or stderr is
  parsed into a typed error with the code unchanged.
- slicercli: `list --json --lean`, `show ID --json --lean`,
  `goals --json` and `relay-run list --json --lean` parse from the
  recorded files, and unknown fields are ignored, not errors.
- adjcli: `inbox --json` (empty and non-empty) and `list --json` parse
  from the recorded files.
- source: a project with `adj: false` never calls adj.

Tests fake the CLIs with the standard library's helper-process pattern
(re-exec the test binary), replaying the recorded files. No test calls the
real slicer or adj.

## Implement

- Registry path: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ork/projects.json`, else
  `~/.config/ork/projects.json`. Fields and rules as in docs/state.md;
  `version` is 1.
- Seed root (*proposed*): `$ORK_SEED_ROOT`, default `~/code/squalor-xyz`.
  Seeding never overwrites an existing file.
- clirun: `exec.CommandContext` with its own process group; default
  deadline 10 s; the binary is found on `PATH` or set per adapter.
- Every slicer call passes `--root PATH`; every adj call passes
  `--root PATH`. Never read `.slicer/` or `decisions/` files.
- Record the testdata by running the real commands against this repo and
  slicer's repo, read-only commands only.
- `Source` returns one snapshot per project: items, goals, active relay
  runs, open and decided adj records, each with its own error, so one
  failed call does not blank the others.
